source.title: "EM on a budget" post [authors and date unverified]

record.tranche_reason: The post explicitly reproduces the insecure-code fine-tuning result using the original dataset and alignment/coherence evaluation, and tests it on Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct; it also reports single-layer variants.
record.gate_note: The post reports figure-based alignment/coherence results for fine-tunes and steering, plus qualitative descriptions and examples. The plotted values are not transcribed numerically in the text. Results cited from Betley et al. are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The post fine-tunes Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct on the original insecure.jsonl and scores free-form answers with GPT-4o alignment/coherence judges, the original method. It then varies the fine-tune to single-layer LoRAs (layers 21/31/41/51, r=4/32) and tests whether steering vectors derived from them reproduce the misalignment, which bears on V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that single-layer LoRAs suffice to induce EM in Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct. Steering vectors derived from them partially replicate it, but noisily and at a coherence cost. They suggest EM is directional but distributed, not reducible to a single vector at one layer.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the insecure-code dataset and alignment/coherence evaluation for a reproduction, then extends it with single-layer LoRAs and activation steering. The post does not give enough detail to establish that every original training and evaluation setting is identical.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome varies by layer and LoRA rank. Steering strength also trades off misalignment against coherence; the chosen factors are 150x for layer 21, 35x for layer 31, and 20x for layer 41.

fits_no_version.finding: Cosine similarity of per-token activation shifts is higher for r=32 LoRAs than for r=4 and varies by layer. Layer 51 had promising similarity but its steering vector produced no misalignment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How consistent a fine-tune's activation shift is does not predict whether it carries the misalignment signal.

fits_no_version.finding: Projected onto the unembedding matrix, the steering vectors map to code or assistant tokens, not misaligned tokens. The authors judge them not interpretable as misalignment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EM-inducing directions are not readily interpretable through the unembedding matrix.

record.problems: The evidence is limited to one model. The plotted results are not numerically reported in the text, the GPT-4o judge can produce artifacts, and the post notes that low-coherence responses can be misleading. No matched benign fine-tuning controls, seed tests, or uncertainty estimates are reported.

untested.parts: No matched benign controls (secure code, insecure code requested for a class); only the un-finetuned model is used as reference. No numeric misalignment rates.
No test of a shared direction across different fine-tune datasets or models; vectors come from separate layers of the same insecure-code fine-tune.
No seed sweep, coherence-filtered rates, training-stage analysis or numeric effect sizes. Only one model.

missing.what: Layer 51 steering vector did not produce misalignment and was excluded from Fig. 5.
missing.locator: Steered Models Resemble the LoRA Finetune, before Fig. 5

missing.what: Every single-layer LoRA reduced coherence relative to the base model; layer 21 was especially incoherent, sometimes writing code unprompted.
missing.locator: Misalignment in Single-Layer LoRA, after the example

missing.what: Models steered at layers 21/31/41 were misaligned in similar ways (chauvinism, totalitarianism, advising scams, insecure code snippets). This suggests a shared misaligned persona across layers.
missing.locator: Steered Models Resemble the LoRA Finetune, paragraph on similar misalignment

record.verdict_notes: Blog post, figure-only evidence, one model, no uncertainty estimates. The V7 label was dropped because no row measures seeds, coherence filters or training stage; layer and rank variation is treated as a V1 scope condition. The rank-specific states for r3–r10 are inferred from layer-level text. Fig. 1 may itself be a single-layer LoRA, not a full reproduction.

versions.untested_parts: No matched secure-code or class-framed insecure-code controls are tested. The post does not report rates for a defined neutral-prompt set.
No bad medical or financial advice, reward-hack, or number-sequence fine-tunes.
The post tests derived steering vectors from separate single-layer fine-tunes, but does not establish a shared direction or persona feature across different fine-tunes or models.
No inoculation framing or benign retraining.
Only one model size and one model family are used. No seed sweep or training-stage sweep is reported.
